title: Data Cloud for Marketing
html:
Marketing is where most Data 360 initiatives go live first: unified profiles and segments become personalized journeys, engagement data flows back to enrich the profile, and the loop closes. This phase covers Marketing Cloud Engagement and Account Engagement integration, journey data sources, segment-driven sends, and the marketing personas/consent patterns.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Explain the data flow between Data 360 and Marketing Cloud (segments → data extensions → journeys).
  • Configure a journey entry source backed by a Data 360 segment activation.
  • Bring engagement data (opens/clicks/conversions) back for profile enrichment and insight.
  • Use consent categories and suppression in the marketing loop.
  • Identify the Data 360 marketing permission sets and their scope.

1. The Marketing 360 loop

text
[ Data 360 unified profile ] --segment--> [ Activation -> SFMC data extension ]
                                            |        |
               enrichment <-- engagement --+        +--> Journey Builder send
           (opens/clicks feed back)                   +--> next segment

Two directions matter:

  1. Outbound (activate): segments + attributes → SFMC data extension → journey/campaign entry.
  2. Inbound (ingest): MC engagement data extensions (sends, opens, clicks, conversions) → Data 360, where they join the profile, power engagement insights, and improve the next segment.

Marketing data is usually the first dataset teams unify because it is high-volume and already structured. The exam expects you to know: MC connector (ingest) and Marketing activations (egress) are separate configurations, and both are permission- and consent-aware.

2. Segment → Journey (the standard pattern)

  1. Build the segment (Phase 6). Add the attributes the journey needs.
  2. Create an activation to Marketing Cloud Engagement (Phase 7). Choose refresh (scheduled daily is typical; real-time when the trigger is moment-based).
  3. In Journey Builder, choose "Data 360 segment" (formerly Data Cloud audience) as the entry source and point it at the synchronized data extension.
  4. Design the journey (email + SMS + engagement decision splits referencing the segment's attributes).
  5. Monitor the journey + activation runs.

Golden rules:

  • Entry source = the data extension fed by the activation. Members enter when the activation refreshes/qualifies them.
  • Attributes carried are what decide personalization and branches (e.g. Total_Spend thresholds, Churn_Score).
  • Refresh cadence must match the journey's promise (a "next 24 hours" journey needs a frequent refresh, not weekly).
  • Never build the journey against the editable live data extension without governance — rename/version data extensions on schema change and let the activation update the sync version.

3. Engagement data back into Data 360

The Marketing Cloud connector brings data extensions (sends, opens, clicks, bounces, conversions, and custom extension data) into Data 360 as DLOs. From there:

  • map to Engagement/MarketingActivity DMOs,
  • enrich the unified profile (open-rate, last-click, lifetime engagement),
  • feed engagement insights and predictive models (Phase 13),
  • re-enter segmentation to include/exclude engaged profiles.

The exam loop question is almost always: "After a send, how do we know which members responded, so the next segment excludes non-engagers?" → bring send/click data back via the MC connector, map it, and use the resulting attributes in the segment.

4. Marketing Cloud Account Engagement (Pardot)

For B2B, Account Engagement (MC AE) syncs prospects and automation rules. Data 360 can ingest AE activities (visits, form submissions) and activate segments to AE prospect fields/segments. The same consent and activation rules apply; the AE path is usually complementary to the MCE data-extension path rather than a replacement.

Personas & permissions

The Data 360 permission sets you will assign to marketing users:

Permission setScope
Data 360 Marketing AdminCreate segments and activations; manage data spaces for marketing
Data 360 Marketing ViewerView segments/activations and run metrics (viewing only)
Data 360 AdminFull platform administration (ingestion, modeling, security)

Marketing Admins can build and publish audiences but cannot administer ingestion/modeling — splitting duties is a governance baseline the exam expects you to articulate.

5. Consent in the marketing loop

Marketing activation is the strictest consent arena:

  1. Consent categories — Email, SMS, Advertising are distinct categories on the unified profile.
  2. Capture — opt-in/out comes from forms (Web/API) and is ingested or set via consent objects (Phase 11).
  3. Enforce — activations suppress by category; journeys must honor the same flags.
  4. Honor the unsubscribe — sending into an SMTP suppression/opt-out must persist back into Data 360 so the profile reflects it (suppressed = true), otherwise the next segment rebuilds a doomed audience.

The lab models capture in ConsentManagementService (Consent_Preference__c) and enforcement in ActivationSyncService — you saw the suppression math in Phase 7.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Draw the marketing loop

Trace a win-back campaign end-to-end: source data → segment → activation → data extension → journey → send → opens/clicks back into Data 360 → updated segment. Label each hop with the Data 360 or MC feature used.

Exercise 2: Journey entry decision

Scenario: an airline wants a post-booking "upgrade offer" journey to members who booked in the last 48h and are Gold+. Choose: which segment, which attributes, MCE or MCAE, refresh cadence, and consent category. Justify each choice.

Exercise 3: Engagement feedback

Write the conceptual mapping for send_events DLO → Engagement DMO fields (member id, timestamp, action). State which unified-profile attribute the closes/clicks should produce, and which segment criteria use it.

Exercise 4: Lab

Extend ConsentManagementServiceTest with a "unsubscribe propagates to activation suppression" test: member suppresses via consent update, then ActivationSyncService excludes them.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Marketing Cloud Engagement (MCE)SFMC — journey/campaign platform receiving Data 360 segments as data extensions.
Marketing cloud connectorData 360 connector that ingests MC engagement data back into DLOs/DMOs.
Journey entry sourceThe data source (segment-activated data extension) that starts members into a journey.
Data extensionSFMC storage created/updated by a Data 360 activation.
Account Engagement (AE)B2B marketing automation (Pardot) that syncs prospects and activities.
Consent categoryA channel-based opt-in flag (Email, SMS, Advertising).
Data 360 Marketing AdminPermission set enabling marketing users to build/run segments and activations.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can trace segment → activation → data extension → journey → feedback loop.
  • I can set up a journey entry source for a Data 360 segment and pick refresh cadence.
  • I can explain how engagement data re-enters the profile and improves segments.
  • I can enforce marketing consent categories and honor unsubscribes.
  • I can name the marketing Data 360 permission sets and their limits.
